waypoints.name: Whiskey Bend Trailhead
waypoints.note: Start of the Elwha River Trail; From Whiskey Bend the route follows the Elwha River Trail roughly 16+ miles south to the Hayes River area before leaving trail for the class 2 scramble to Norton's summit.

waypoints.name: Mary's Falls Camp
waypoints.note: Established backcountry campsite beside the Elwha River with reliable water; roughly the halfway point to Elkhorn and a common overnight stop for the long approach.
waypoints.directions: Follow the Elwha River Trail south up the valley through forest, past the Lillian River, to Mary's Falls Camp beside the river at about 8.8 miles.

waypoints.name: Elkhorn Guard Station
waypoints.note: Historic 1911 backcountry patrol cabin and grassy river-flat camp; last reliably maintained camp before leaving the main Elwha corridor toward Norton.
waypoints.directions: Continue up the Elwha River Trail past Canyon Camp to the historic Elkhorn Guard Station and its grassy river-flat camp.

waypoints.name: Hayes River Guard Station
waypoints.note: Elwha River Trail meets the Hayes River here (16.1 mi from Whiskey Bend per NPS); climbers leave the maintained trail near this junction and head up the Hayes River drainage toward Norton's east slopes.
waypoints.directions: Continue up the Elwha River Trail about 4.5 miles to the Hayes River Guard Station, where the Hayes River joins the Elwha.

waypoints.name: Off-trail ascent below Norton's east face
waypoints.note: No path or cairns beyond Hayes River — dense slide alder and devil's club in the lower brush belt give way to open Class 2 heather/talus higher up; the east aspect gains about 3,200 ft in under a mile, so route-find carefully in fog or low visibility.

itinerary.cal: Since the Olympic Hot Springs Road washed out in November 2017, vehicle access has ended at Madison Falls, adding roughly 7 miles each way of road walking/biking before the old Whiskey Bend trailhead; check NPS Wilderness Trail Conditions for washouts beyond Elkhorn, and get a wilderness camping permit — best conditions are June through August.

days.note: From the trailhead (Madison Falls, since flood damage in November 2017 washed out the Olympic Hot Springs Road and closed it to vehicles beyond there) follow the old road bed and then the Elwha River Trail south through second-growth and old-growth forest. Grade is gentle and the trail is well-graded, so this is mostly a long valley walk.
days.title: Backpack in to lower Elwha camp

days.note: A shorter day continuing up-valley along the Elwha River Trail to the Hayes River patrol cabin/camp area, which sits almost directly below Mount Norton's steep east face. Check current NPS trail-condition reports first — sections between Elkhorn and Hayes River have had flood/landslide damage in recent years.
days.title: Continue to Hayes River
days.objective: Camp near Hayes River Guard Station

days.note: Leave the heavy gear at Hayes River camp and climb the steep, brushy east aspect (about 3,200 ft of gain in under a mile per the peak's official description) to the upper ridge, then follow class 2 talus/heather slopes to the summit. Out-and-back to the same camp same day.
days.title: Summit push

schedule.label: Leave Hayes River camp
schedule.detail: Light day pack, leave tents/food cache set up.

schedule.label: Start the steep east-side climb
schedule.detail: Brushy, unmaintained, steep — pick the path of least resistance up open timber and heather bands.

schedule.label: Gain the summit ridge
schedule.detail: Terrain eases to class 2 talus and heather.

schedule.label: Reach the summit (6,319 ft)
schedule.detail: Views over the Bailey Range and Elwha/Hayes drainages.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent line; steep terrain is slower and harder to reverse than it looks.

days.objective: Climb Mount Norton's east side and return to camp

days.note: Retrace the Elwha River Trail (and road-walk/bike section from Madison Falls if the road closure is still in effect) all the way back to the car. A long but flat-grade day.
days.title: Hike out

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 4-day trip, roughly 38 miles and ~5,000+ ft round trip: two long valley-trail days in, one steep off-trail summit day from a Hayes River camp, and one long day out.
